title: Bounded reachability implies simulation
statement: Let $A$ be an instruction program on $m$ registers, with control states in $\Lambda$, and let an oracle answer Boolean queries to $d$ deciders. Fix an initial state $l_0$, Boolean input $x$, states $l,l'\in\Lambda$, register values $v:\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\to\bbn$, output word $o$, register $r$, and integers $L,W$ with $0\le W$ and $L\le W$. Form the initial and final configurations with states $l$ and $l'$, respectively, phase at its start, input head at position one, every register tape storing the binary expansion of its assigned value with head at zero, and output $o$. If the program reaches the final configuration from the initial one and, at every strictly earlier time, is at an ordinary (non-call) state with register $r$'s head at some position $q$ satisfying $-1\le q\le L$, then the run is a simulation to the final configuration in which every strictly earlier configuration is an ordinary state and every register head position lies between $-1$ and $W$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: The register program $A$, oracle, and initial control state $l_0$
The stated bounded reachability property, including ordinary states and register-$r$ head positions in $[-1,L]$ at all earlier times
